messages:
ryan-sales: Heads-up — Acme trial is ramping traffic (sudden demo spike) and they're seeing intermittent 502/503s. They want this fixed before EOD or we risk losing the deal. Can we swarm? :pray:
maria-se: on it. Can you paste the exact error lines and approximate qps?
ryan-sales: QPS peaked ~280/s, baseline 60/s. Customer logs show HTTP 502: 'upstream read error' and 503 'service unavailable' around 12:13pm UTC.
alex.shepherd: Sending logs request to the ingest cluster now. @jake-oncall can you check the autoscaler logs for `eval-pool`?
jake-oncall: grabbing autoscaler logs. Quick note — our burstpool limits for this org are 2 nodes and the policy has a 90s cool-down. If ramp is fast we might hit queueing.
dina-support: Customer also reported long tail latency before the 5xx. Might be KV cache misses causing expensive recalc. Asking them for prompt samples now.
deploy-bot: [deploy] New canary deployed to eval-pool at 2026-03-21T12:05:02Z by infra-ci.
jake-oncall: autoscaler log excerpt: ```2026-03-21T12:12:59Z INFO scale_attempt: desired=10 current=6 reason=queue_depth>80; 2026-03-21T12:13:40Z WARN scale_rate_limited: cooldown=90s; 2026-03-21T12:14:30Z INFO scaled_up: new=8```
alex.shepherd: So scale started but only gained 2 nodes in the window. Queue depth hit 120 requests and backend started returning 502 during prewarm. Need faster burst capacity or temporary routing to alternate region.
maria-se: Can we temporarily increase burstpool to 5 for this org? That would absorb the spike. What's the cost implication — I'll fwd to sales for approval.
jake-oncall: We can bump to 5 but it's a manual override. It will provision GPUs, ~10-12 min cold start for new instances; in past we've mitigated by routing to standby region with prewarmed nodes (us-west-2).\ryan-sales: 10–12 min is risky — customer is demoing in 8. Any faster option?
dina-support: Two quick mitigations: 1) Enable traffic fallback to a smaller quantized model variant in the same pool (lower throughput per request but faster start), 2) Route a percent of requests to hosted fallback that has headroom. Both are config flips, near-instant.
alex.shepherd: Agreed. Recommend: enable fallback route (20%) to hosted, and enable low-cost quantized variant for remaining traffic. That should reduce queue depth quickly and stop 5xx.
maria-se: I'll ask legal for approval on fallback to hosted for a trial — it's within our standard eval terms. Ryan can you confirm the customer will accept short routing to hosted?\ryan-sales: Customer OK with temporary fallback as long as data isn't persisted and they sign SSO/contract next week.
jake-oncall: Implemented rollout: `redwood route set eval-org --fallback-hosted=20% --model-variant=quant-8bit` — done, traffic split active.
deploy-bot: [route] eval-org: fallback-hosted=20% applied at 2026-03-21T12:16:04Z by alex.shepherd.
alex.shepherd: Monitoring: within 90s queue depth dropped from 120 -> 30, 5xx rate down to <1%. Latency tail improved.
dina-support: Still seeing a few 502s tied to one pod that OOM'd. We should drain and recreate it. @jake-oncall can you cordon/replace?
jake-oncall: cordoned and recreated pod eval-worker-42; logs show `OOMKilled` likely due to a memory leak in that older canary. Rolling it out of pool.
\alm: reaction :thumbsup: (not a real user, just demonstrating reactions)
maria-se: Great. Ryan — please capture customer sentiment and we'll include this in the post-demo follow-up. Also propose reserved capacity for predictable demos (Dedicated) — note on pricing we can offer a short-term trial discount.yan-sales: Will do, customer impressed with the quick mitigation. Thanks team — please capture the steps so I can include in the handoff doc.
dina-support: I'll paste a short postmortem into the ticket: 1) rapid ramp + cooldown delayed autoscale -> queueing; 2) single OOM pod amplified 5xx; 3) mitigation: enabled hosted fallback (20%), switched to quantized variant, replaced OOM pod.
alex.shepherd: saving config snippets and logs to the ticket. Follow-up action: set org burstpool auto-allow to 4 for eval orgs by default, and add alert for queue depth > 60 sustained 60s.
jake-oncall: filing infra task for burstpool policy change and shorter scale cooldown for eval pools.yan-sales: excellent — customer demo proceeding. I owe snacks. :tada:
